description:
Advances: ancora.parsing

Ancora 1.0 cannot represent a subject pruned under an authorizing ADR. append_only.ex:82 authorizes a requirement deletion only when the accepted ADR's affects: names the deleted requirement id or its subject id, while DecisionParser.Affects resolves affects: strictly against the CURRENT index — a pruned subject and its requirement ids are gone from that index by definition, so the same ADR that satisfies the append-only guard emits adr/affects_unresolved at error, persistently, on every future spec.validate run. No corpus shape satisfies both rules. This is a spec-design gap, not a code bug: ancora.parsing's requirement (that an affects id not in the corpus shall emit adr/affects_unresolved) mandates the behavior, so the fix is a spec edit with clause accounting plus implementation — e.g. a retires:/retired-affects vocabulary the resolver exempts and the append-only guard accepts as authorization — and a 1.0.x release.

Surfaced by the M7 Engage migration (ancora-yzu.23), which prunes spec.system under its migration ADR. Interim posture consumers carry until this lands: severities adr/affects_unresolved: info in the consumer config, recorded in the migration ADR (trailers cannot price it — the finding is persistent, trailers are commit-scoped). Consumers that took the demotion should re-tighten to the registry default when adopting the release that closes this ticket. Not an epic child: the demotion unblocks all remaining migrations (M7-M9), so nothing in ancora-yzu depends on this fix.

Status note (2026-09-03): the 'Not an epic child' sentence above predates this ticket being re-homed under ancora-xla. It is a child now. Blocked by ancora-v1n because both tickets redefine what an ADR affects: entry authorizes; the retirement vocabulary must be built on the authorization rule v1n settles.

Ruling needed before code moves (Manuel): what vocabulary lets an accepted ADR name a retired subject or requirement id so that cold spec.validate accepts it and the append-only guard treats it as authorization?
Recommended default from the ticket: a retires: field on the ADR (alongside affects:) whose ids the Affects resolver exempts from adr/affects_unresolved and which append_only.ex accepts as authorization for the named deletions. Requires a new must in ancora.parsing with clause accounting, and a 1.0.x release note.
Worker: if no comment on this ticket records a ruling when you start, park and ask. Do not choose on Manuel's behalf and do not implement more than one option.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: tagged tests for the new ancora.parsing requirement plus existing tags under ancora.parsing for affects resolution and append-only authorization (test/ancora/decision_parser_test.exs, test/ancora/append_only_test.exs)
- Behaviors to demonstrate: (1) a corpus that deletes a whole subject under an accepted ADR naming it in the retirement vocabulary passes mix spec.validate cold with zero adr/affects_unresolved and zero append/requirement_deleted; (2) an id that is neither in the index nor in the retirement vocabulary still emits adr/affects_unresolved at error; (3) the vocabulary appears in the spec.init decision template so new adopters see it
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: mix test --stale or explicitly named test files, plus mix spec.validate; no full suite mid-iteration.
  - Final tier: immediately before IMPLEMENTED, run-until-green: mix compile --warnings-as-errors && mix test && mix format --check-formatted && mix deps.unlock --check-unused && mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission
  - Verifier tier: mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission plus tagged and --stale selections only; do NOT run the full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test that exercises that production path.
  - Fixture hygiene: one TmpGitRepo per test, no shared temp dirs, async only where the fixture allows.
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh for every touched callable surface. Drift, growth, and shrink clear only through substantive requirement or scenario edits in the same diff, never through a Spec-Ack trailer.
  - Every conditional clause covered by a test.
- proves: a pruned subject under an authorizing ADR validates clean without any severity demotion or tombstone files.

- .spec/specs/ancora.gate.spec.md (added 2026-09-03 by the orchestrator. This list already permits lib/ancora/append_only.ex, which ancora.gate governs, so any edit there raises drift that only a substantive edit to this spec can clear. Acknowledgment edits only: substantive requirement or scenario updates that clear drift, growth or shrink caused by THIS ticket's own changes. Never weaken a must, never delete a requirement.)
- Any spec whose stated rule THIS ticket's change makes false, for the sole purpose of correcting that statement in the same diff. Recorded after ancora-v1n shipped a corpus holding two scenarios that predicted opposite outcomes from identical input, because the spec stating the old rule was withheld from its Allowed list and the worker retagged around the conflict instead of flagging it. If you find a requirement anywhere in .spec/ that your change falsifies, fixing it here is in scope and expected. Say so in your completion record.

SCOPE ADDITION (orchestrator, 2026-09-03 19:55), assigned here rather than filed as a new ticket, because this ticket already owns the append-only authorization domain and is sequenced immediately after ancora-v1n.

The ancora-v1n re-verification found that lib/ancora/finding.ex:234 and :239 still render remediation hints telling the user to "add an accepted ADR whose affects: names the requirement or its subject". After ancora-v1n lands, following that advice with a subject id will NOT work. The tool would actively mislead a user at the exact moment they hit the guard and go looking for help, which is worse than saying nothing.

Fix both render clauses so the advice names the requirement id only, consistent with ancora.gate.two_append_guards as ancora-v1n leaves it and with the retirement vocabulary this ticket introduces. Keep it to the wording; do not restructure the finding renderer.

Added to Allowed touches: lib/ancora/finding.ex (the two append-family render clauses only; no other finding rendering).

The sibling occurrence in NOTICE line 42 repeats the same stale phrasing and has been assigned to ancora-xla.8, which already owns NOTICE.

SECOND SCOPE ADDITION (orchestrator, 2026-09-03 20:50), found by the ancora-v1n auditor while probing, and assigned here because this ticket already has the two clauses in Allowed touches for the stale-hint correction above. Same two clauses, same edit.

Pre-existing message bug, predating the whole epic. lib/ancora/finding.ex:232-240 renders the id as `"#{s(ctx)}.#{req(ctx)}"`, composing subject and requirement, while lib/ancora/append_only.ex:89 and :99 already pass an ALREADY-QUALIFIED requirement id. So a real finding message reads "alpha.alpha.two deleted", with the subject doubled.

It is invisible today only by luck: test/ancora/append_only_test.exs:26 asserts a substring that survives the doubling. Nothing else checks the rendered message.

Fix it in the same edit as the stale-hint wording. Either stop composing in the renderer or stop qualifying at the call site, whichever reads better, but do not do both and do not add a field. The ancora-v1n auditor established while probing this that Ancora.Finding has NO :requirement field: lib/ancora/finding.ex:127 accepts :requirement in attrs, uses it only to render the message, and drops it, and the struct at :11 carries code, subject, file, message, severity, severity_source. Do not add one; it is a shipped struct behind 30 finding codes.

Add an assertion that pins the full rendered message rather than a surviving substring, so the doubling cannot come back invisibly.

Reasoning: The verifier's FAIL is correct and I am upholding it, and I am promoting one of its Notes to a Gap.

Gap 1 confirmed (verifier's, unchanged). .spec/decisions/README.md:5-7 says "Only an accepted ADR that names the exact requirement id authorizes deleting that requirement or downgrading it from `must` to `should`." This diff falsifies the deletion half, and the falsifying proof is in the diff: test/ancora/append_only_test.exs:95 calls write_adr(root, "retire", "accepted", ["alpha"], ["alpha"]) — affects and retires both hold the bare subject id, no requirement id anywhere — and asserts no append/requirement_deleted. Line 3-4 also lists frontmatter as `id`, `status`, `date`, `affects:` only, so `retires:` is undocumented for anyone authoring an ADR in this repo. The counterpart priv/spec_init/decisions/README.md.eex:6-9 WAS updated with the guidance, so the scaffold teaches the field and the repo's own copy denies it. .spec/decisions/** is an explicit Allowed touch, so the fix is in scope. The file has no ADR frontmatter, so the parser skips it and spec.check stays green on a false statement.

Gap 2, promoted from the verifier's advisory Note. The verifier is factually right that names_retirement?/3 survives a prefix mutation; I reproduced it and it is worse than reported. I do not agree it is a Note. The requirement this ticket exists to add, ancora.parsing.retirement_vocabulary, states "An exact requirement id shall authorize only that requirement's deletion, while a subject id shall authorize deletion of every requirement that belonged to that subject." Exactness and subject-boundedness are the defining words of the new must, not implementation detail. The verifier applied precisely that standard to the affects: side in this same pass (mutation-proven, 3 failures) and then applied a weaker one — "both real clauses are individually proven" — to the new vocabulary. Individual clause proof shows a clause exists; it does not show it is bounded. That is the distinction ancora-v1n was bounced twice to establish.

Measured, in a disposable copy of the worktree, never in the worktree itself:
- Baseline: `mix test test/ancora/append_only_test.exs test/ancora/decision_parser_test.exs` → 29 tests, 0 failures.
- Mutation A, requirement branch: `requirement_id in retires` → `Enum.any?(retires, &String.starts_with?(requirement_id, &1))`. Result: 29 tests, 0 failures. Survives.
- Mutation B, subject branch: `subject_id in retires` → `Enum.any?(retires, &String.starts_with?(subject_id, &1))`. Result: 29 tests, 0 failures. Survives.
Two independent loosenings of the new vocabulary, both silent. append_only_test.exs:153 misses them because "alpha.two" does not start with "alpha.one".

What a prefix match would then authorize, concretely: an accepted ADR carrying `retires: ["alpha"]` would authorize deleting `alphabet.one`, a requirement in a different subject that the ADR never names. That is retiring a requirement nobody named, the same class ancora-v1n was bounced twice for, and it is ordinary in a dotted-id corpus — this repo alone would have `ancora.gate` matching a future `ancora.gateway`.

Bounce reason: fold both into one commit.
1. .spec/decisions/README.md. Add `retires:` to the frontmatter list at line 3-4, and correct the sentence at 5-7 so it states the rule this ticket actually ships: an accepted ADR's `affects:` naming the exact requirement id authorizes deleting or downgrading it; `retires:` naming that requirement id or its subject id authorizes deletion only. Abbreviated, not false; same edit if you are in there.

Two subjects sharing a prefix, `alpha` and `alphabet`, each with one must. On HEAD remove alpha's spec file and drop alphabet's requirement, then write_adr(root, "retire", "accepted", ["alpha"], ["alpha"]). Assert append/requirement_deleted fires with message =~ "alphabet.one deleted", and refute any finding matching "alpha.one deleted" so the subject retirement it IS supposed to authorize stays authorized. No new fixture helper; write_spec, spec_with_reqs, spec_without_req and the 5-arity write_adr already in the file are enough.

I measured that test before ordering it, run both ways. With it added: clean HEAD → 30 tests, 0 failures. Mutation A → that test fails, alone. Mutation B → that test fails, alone. One test, ~20 lines, kills both loosenings. No harness.
